working_title: Predictive skill can misidentify information transfer in hierarchical ecological data
one_sentence_claim: When ecological prediction is evaluated against a pooled reference, layer identity can be credited to the contextual information under study; matching the reference to the claim separates layer identity from within-layer transfer.

positioning.odsp_role: implementation of explicit held-out score decomposition and reproducible audits

required_sequence: problem: predictive improvement does not identify which information caused the improvement
mechanism: pooled reference conflates layer identity with within-layer context
known-truth result: BOP-scale layer effects yield near-certain pooled-reference false transfer while conditioned decomposition controls error
fresh real-data result: Palmer Penguins reverses from positive pooled morphology gain to negative species-conditioned morphology gain
scope control: pooled reference remains appropriate when identity itself is the claim, as in Snapshot Serengeti
conclusion: reference information must match the information-transfer claim

paragraph_roles: ecologists often interpret held-out predictive improvement as evidence that newly added context transfers
hierarchical identity creates a hidden comparator problem; introduce the Buteo buteo motivating decomposition without treating it as confirmatory
define explicit-layer and proxy-layer failure modes and state why group CV alone cannot fix a reference-definition error
state preregistered known-truth and real-data tests and the falsification/withdrawal logic

core_equations.proxy_case: when context X correlates with omitted layer L, S(X)-S(pool) can be positive even if true within-layer context information is zero
core_equations.score: held-out mean log predictive probability; larger is better

methods_sections: Claim-aligned reference principle and additive decomposition
Population-mean decision rule and few-cluster correction

bop_population.role: do not use as a positive population-mean result

serengeti.interpretation: pooled identity-blind reference is appropriate because species identity itself is the claimed transferred information

panels: explicit-layer case: full model versus pooled reference conflates layer and context
proxy-layer case: context correlated with omitted layer inherits layer signal
anchor A/B/C false-positive rates for pooled versus decomposed context
factorial heatmap of pooled false-transfer rate
factorial heatmap of decomposed false-transfer rate
power and bias for genuine context effects
Palmer Penguins naive pooled gain versus layer and corrected context components with CR1+t2 intervals

tables.purpose: predeclared empirical roles and comparator semantics

discussion_structure: predictive validation protects against overfitting but does not identify the information source
group cross-validation cannot repair a comparator that omits a relevant layer
conditioning is claim-dependent rather than universally preferable; Serengeti defines the boundary
implications for SDMs and hierarchical ecological prediction, including esdm
limitations: Stage 2 is triangulation rather than literature prevalence; few layers limit superpopulation inference; decomposition is not causal identification
prohibited_claims: ODSP is a new ecological prediction framework as the central paper contribution
BOP shows a positive population-mean context transfer after the four-cluster correction
the two Stage-2 failure-eligible systems estimate the prevalence of the problem in ecology
AUC is generally inferior to log score
conditioning on a layer establishes causality
all hierarchical models should condition on the same layer

stage4.if_done: published-study reanalyses are scope-expansion evidence only and cannot alter the Stage1/Stage2 core conclusion
